Signal: Direction level + step clock to an inherited driver
Controller resource: Timer output (step) + GPIO (direction), via 74HCT541 level-up
Items: MOT1 resistance-to-pour gauge
Notes: The VID66-08 is on the GAUGE ASSEMBLY, not the main board - CONFIRMED by opening the machine and reading the part off that board, which also fits the 9-conductor harness closing only if the driver is local. Note the board silkscreens it U8 where the circuit diagram says U9; the manual has U8 and U9 swapped. If that board is retained the driver is inherited and the controller drives logic lines, not motor phases. Step clock needs a timer channel: a needle has inertia and an uneven rate reads as stutter. DRIVE LEVEL: the VID6608 datasheet puts Vih at 3.15 V min and Vil at 1.35 V max as absolute figures across its whole 4.5-5.5 V supply range. Its prose says the inputs carry level shifters so the part may run at a higher VDD than the logic driving it, but that decouples the threshold from the motor rail without lowering it. So a 3.3 V controller has 150 mV of margin at best and needs level shifting or a Voh guarantee checked against 3.15 V. In this design the five driver lines go through a 74HCT541 level-up (D19, Chosen), which clears the threshold. The pin allocation lists them as plain GPIO (PD0 PD1 PD4 PD5 PD6; roles not recorded), which does not provide the timer step clocks this row asks for (to confirm). Rising edge steps 1/12 degree of shaft rotation fixed in silicon; 450 ns min pulse; 100 ns direction setup; 20 ns glitch filter; speed ceiling 7.2 kHz, quoted against VID29 movements that MOT1/MOT2 have not been identified as. See docs/sunbeam-em7000/connector-pinouts.md
